keyframes.prompt: Vertical 2:3 nature photo of a cutaway view of the forest floor at the base of an old oak tree, showing the part above the ground and the part below the ground at the same time. The ground surface is a straight horizontal line at about one third of the frame height from the top. Above the ground: the wide base of a rough grey-brown oak trunk in the center, a thick layer of fallen brown oak leaves on the ground, and a soft out-of-focus green forest behind. Below the ground: a clean side cutaway of dark brown, soft, moist leaf mold and crumbly humus with small pieces of rotten wood and old leaf fragments. A few thin roots spread out only just below the ground surface. In the center of the soil, at about 60 percent of the frame height from the top, three small pearly white oval beetle eggs lie together in a small hollow. Each egg is about one fortieth of the frame height long. Nothing else is in the soil. Soft warm daylight, everything clearly lit, sharp focus. Keep everything important away from the left and right edges. No text, no watermark.

Edit this image. Keep the ground, the soil cutaway, the oak trunk, the leaves, background, lighting and camera angle exactly the same. The three eggs are now empty, torn, see-through white egg shells in the same spot. One tiny newly hatched rhinoceros beetle grub lies curled in a C shape right next to the empty shells. It is soft and creamy white, with a small pale orange head and tiny legs, about one sixteenth of the frame height long. Only one grub. No text, no watermark.

Edit this image. Keep the ground, the soil cutaway, the oak trunk, the empty egg shells, background, lighting and camera angle exactly the same. It is creamy white and slightly see-through, with a shiny orange-brown head, six short legs near the head, a row of small orange breathing spots along each side, and a darker grey rear end. Its curled body is about one fifth of the frame height tall. Only one grub. No text, no watermark.

Inside the chamber, the same grub is now a prepupa: it lies straight and upright with its head toward the top of the chamber, its skin is wrinkled and yellowish cream, and it does not move. Only one prepupa. No text, no watermark. Show the prepupa from the side, its head at the top facing left and its back facing right.

Edit this image. Keep everything exactly the same, including the ground, the soil cutaway, the oak trunk, the pupal chamber, background, lighting and camera angle. The prepupa is now a male Japanese rhinoceros beetle pupa standing upright in the same chamber, head at the top facing left and its back facing right, seen from the side like the prepupa. It is shiny amber orange-brown, with a long curved horn on its head, a short horn on its thorax, legs and wing pads folded against its body, and a ringed abdomen. A crumpled pale shed skin lies at the bottom of the chamber. Only one pupa. No text, no watermark.

Edit this image. Keep everything exactly the same, including the ground, the soil cutaway, the oak trunk, the pupal chamber, the shed skin, background, lighting and camera angle.
